chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked him about a man who brings dirhams to the money-changer, who says to him, 'I will take from you one hundred [dirhams] for one hundred and ten, or for one hundred and five, until he is satisfied with what he wants.' When he is done, he places the excess dirhams as a dinar or gold. Then he says to him, 'I have returned the sale to you, and I am only trading with you on this, because the first [sale] is not valid,' or he did not say that, and he placed gold in place of the dirhams. He said, 'If the execution of the sale is upon the permissible, then there is no harm with that.' I said, 'And if he places copper coins in place of the gold?' He said, 'I do not know what the copper coins are.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell currency for a higher price of the same currency to settle a debt in a different form of money?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the mechanism of *bay' al-kali' bi'l-kali'* (deferred-for-deferred sale) as a practical financial instrument used by money-changers to circumvent riba (usury) while satisfying creditors. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the transaction provided the underlying exchange is lawful, highlighting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the substance of the deal over its formal structure. The uncertainty regarding 'fulus' (copper coins) reflects the historical context of currency debasement and the varying scholarly opinions on whether such low-value coins constitute valid currency for these transactions.
